emails.subject: URGENT: Missing Essential Documents in ISF - Site 2047 - Protocol CT-2023-089
emails.body:
Dear Dr. Chen,

During our routine ISF review in preparation for the upcoming sponsor audit scheduled for April 8-10, 2024, we have identified critical gaps in your Investigator Site File for Protocol CT-2023-089.

The following essential documents are missing or outdated:

1. Dr. Amanda Foster (Sub-Investigator)
   - Current CV (on file dated 2022, >2 years old)
   - Current medical license (expired copy on file, expired 12/31/2023)
   - Updated GCP training certificate (expired 01/15/2024)

2. Dr. Michael Torres (Sub-Investigator)
   - Current CV (on file dated 2021)
   - Current medical license (copy on file expires 03/31/2024 - renewal needed)

Per ICH-GCP E6(R2) Section 8.2, current CVs and medical licenses must be maintained in the ISF for all investigators and sub-investigators conducting study procedures. Our records indicate both Dr. Foster and Dr. Torres have been actively screening and enrolling subjects, with Dr. Foster conducting procedures for 8 subjects and Dr. Torres for 6 subjects since January 2024.

This constitutes a significant regulatory finding that must be addressed immediately. Please provide the following by COB Monday, March 18, 2024:

1. Updated CVs for both sub-investigators (signed and dated within last 2 years)
2. Current, valid medical license copies for both sub-investigators
3. Updated GCP training certificates
4. A corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plan to ensure this does not recur

Failure to provide these documents prior to the audit may result in:
- Major audit finding
- Temporary suspension of enrollment activities
- Potential site closure consideration
- Regulatory reporting requirements

Please confirm receipt of this email and your plan to address these deficiencies immediately.

Best regards,

Jennifer Martinez, MS, RAC
Senior Regulatory Affairs Specialist
ClinTrials Pharmaceuticals
Phone: (555) 234-5678
Email: jennifer.martinez@clintrials-sponsor.com

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Missing Essential Documents in ISF - Site 2047 - Protocol CT-2023-089
emails.body:
Dear Jennifer,

Thank you for bringing this to our attention. I acknowledge receipt of your email and understand the severity of this situation. I apologize for these oversights in our ISF maintenance.

I have immediately contacted both Dr. Foster and Dr. Torres regarding the missing/outdated documentation. Here is our action plan:

Immediate Actions (by EOD today, March 15):
- Both sub-investigators have been notified and are preparing updated CVs
- Dr. Foster has confirmed her medical license was renewed in January 2024; she is obtaining a certified copy from the state medical board
- Dr. Torres is expediting his license renewal application (submitted last week)
- Both are completing updated GCP training modules today

Documentation Timeline:
- Dr. Foster's updated CV and renewed license copy: Monday, March 18 by noon
- Dr. Foster's GCP certificate: Monday, March 18 by EOD
- Dr. Torres's updated CV: Monday, March 18 by noon
- Dr. Torres's renewed license: pending state processing (typically 5-7 business days)

Interim Measures:
- Effective immediately, Dr. Torres will not conduct any study procedures until his renewed license is on file
- Dr. Foster will continue procedures only after all documents are submitted and approved
- I will personally conduct all screening and enrollment activities until documentation is complete

Melissa (our site coordinator, cc'd) is implementing a new tracking system with monthly reminders for document expiration dates to prevent future occurrences. We will have a full CAPA plan drafted by Monday.

My main concern is Dr. Torres's license renewal timing, as this is dependent on the state medical board processing time. Can you advise on how to handle this gap period?

Again, I sincerely apologize for this situation and take full responsibility for the oversight.

Best regards,

Dr. Robert Chen, MD, PhD
Principal Investigator
City Medical Research Center
Phone: (555) 876-5432

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Missing Essential Documents in ISF - Site 2047 - Protocol CT-2023-089
emails.body:
Dr. Chen,

Thank you for your prompt response and action plan. I appreciate your immediate attention to this matter.

Your interim measures are appropriate. To address your question regarding Dr. Torres:

Dr. Torres must be removed from the delegation log and cannot perform ANY study procedures until:
1. His renewed medical license is received and on file in the ISF
2. All other required documents (CV, GCP certificate) are current
3. The sponsor approves his reinstatement to the delegation log

For Dr. Foster, she also cannot resume study activities until ALL three documents are received and approved by our team.

Additional Requirements:
- Please submit a protocol deviation report for any procedures conducted by either sub-investigator while their credentials were expired/outdated
- Review all source documents and CRFs for subjects seen by these sub-investigators since January 1, 2024, to ensure data integrity
- Your CAPA plan should include: root cause analysis, corrective actions, preventive actions, responsible parties, and timeline for implementation

I'm adding David Park (Clinical Operations Director, cc'd) to this thread as he will need to review the deviation reports and CAPA plan.

Revised submission deadline:
- All Dr. Foster documents: Monday, March 18, 2024 by 12:00 PM EST
- Dr. Foster approved to resume: Monday, March 18, 2024 by 5:00 PM EST (pending review)
- Dr. Torres CV and GCP certificate: Monday, March 18, 2024 by 12:00 PM EST
- Dr. Torres license: as soon as received from state board
- Protocol deviation reports: Tuesday, March 19, 2024
- CAPA plan: Tuesday, March 19, 2024

We will conduct a focused review call on Wednesday, March 20 at 2:00 PM EST to discuss the CAPA and ensure readiness for the audit. Calendar invite to follow.

Please confirm you understand these requirements and timeline.

Best regards,

Jennifer Martinez, MS, RAC
Senior Regulatory Affairs Specialist
ClinTrials Pharmaceuticals

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Missing Essential Documents in ISF - Site 2047 - Protocol CT-2023-089 - Deviation Reports and CAPA
emails.body:
Dear Jennifer,

Please find attached the requested protocol deviation reports and CAPA plan for the ISF documentation deficiencies.

Protocol Deviation Summary:
- Dr. Foster: 12 study visits conducted for 8 subjects between January 3 - March 15, 2024 (while CV outdated and license expired)
- Dr. Torres: 9 study visits conducted for 6 subjects between January 8 - March 15, 2024 (while CV outdated and license near expiration)
- All procedures were conducted by qualified, licensed physicians
- No impact on subject safety identified
- All data collected is accurate and verifiable in source documents
- Deviations classified as Major, non-serious

CAPA Plan Highlights:

Root Cause Analysis:
- Lack of systematic tracking for credential expiration dates
- No automated reminder system in place
- Insufficient oversight during staff transitions (previous coordinator departure in December 2023)

Corrective Actions (Completed):
- All sub-investigator credentials updated and filed
- Comprehensive ISF audit completed for all studies at site
- Dr. Torres removed from delegation log pending license renewal

Preventive Actions (Implementation timeline included in attached plan):
- Electronic tracking system implemented with 90-day, 60-day, and 30-day automatic email reminders
- Monthly ISF review checklist instituted (first Monday of each month)
- Quarterly credential verification by PI
- Enhanced onboarding procedures for new site staff
- Annual ISF training for all site personnel

We have also identified and corrected similar issues in our other active protocols (3 additional studies).

Update on Dr. Torres: We contacted the state medical board again today. They confirmed his license renewal will be processed by March 22, 2024. We will submit it immediately upon receipt.

Please review the attached documents and let us know if any additional information is needed before tomorrow's call.

Best regards,

Melissa Johnson, RN, CCRC
Site Coordinator
City Medical Research Center

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Missing Essential Documents in ISF - Site 2047 - Protocol CT-2023-089 - CAPA Accepted
emails.body:
Dr. Chen and Melissa,

Following our productive discussion this afternoon, I am writing to confirm the outcomes of our focused review call.

Deviation Reports: ACCEPTED
The protocol deviation reports have been reviewed and accepted. We concur with your assessment that while these are major deviations from regulatory requirements, there was no impact on subject safety or data integrity. Both sub-investigators were qualified and licensed physicians at the time procedures were performed. These deviations will be documented in our study files and included in our routine regulatory reporting.

CAPA Plan: ACCEPTED with minor modifications
Your CAPA plan is comprehensive and addresses the root causes effectively. We appreciate the proactive approach to implement similar tracking systems across all your active studies. 

Modifications requested:
1. Add verification step: Site monitor to verify credential tracking system during each monitoring visit
2. Include annual certification that all site personnel have completed ISF training
3. Add trigger for immediate notification to sponsor if any credential will expire within 30 days and renewal is not yet confirmed

Please submit the revised CAPA plan incorporating these modifications by Friday, March 22, 2024.

Audit Readiness:
Assuming Dr. Torres's medical license is received and approved by March 25, 2024, and the revised CAPA is submitted as requested, we are confident the site will be audit-ready. The audit will proceed as scheduled April 8-10, 2024.

The auditor has been briefed on this situation and will verify:
- All corrective actions have been implemented
- New tracking system is functional
- All current credentials are valid and properly filed
- Deviation reports are appropriately documented

We appreciate your immediate attention to this matter and transparent communication throughout this process. Your commitment to regulatory compliance and quality is evident in your swift response.

Please continue to keep us updated on Dr. Torres's license status.

Best regards,

David Park, PharmD
Clinical Operations Director
ClinTrials Pharmaceuticals
Phone: (555) 234-5690
Email: david.park@clintrials-sponsor.com
